about: The interior of the right lung: three lobes, the airway tree, the pulmonary arteries and veins, alveolar clusters and the pleura. The branching is a deterministic illustration of three divisions per lobe, not a traced bronchial atlas, the alveoli are drawn many times life size, and nothing here models gas exchange itself; activity is a display index of the engine's own breathing and circulation signals.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

WEST10.label: West JB, Luks AM. West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 10th ed. Wolters Kluwer, 2016.

parts.label: Upper Lobe
parts.summary: Right upper lobe, above the horizontal fissure
parts.function: The right upper lobe lies above the horizontal fissure and takes in the apex of the lung beneath the collarbone. It is supplied by its own lobar bronchus, artery and vein. Air reaches it through its own lobar bronchus. It brightens when breathing is deeper or faster, for example when the exercise level is raised, and dims when breathing is depressed.

drives.note: A lobe is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.
Shallow or slow breathing leaves the lobe less ventilated than at rest.

parts.label: Middle Lobe
parts.summary: Right middle lobe, a wedge between the two fissures
parts.function: The middle lobe is a small wedge on the front of the right lung, between the horizontal and oblique fissures. Only the right lung has one; the left lung's lingula is its counterpart. Air reaches it through its own lobar bronchus. It brightens when breathing is deeper or faster, for example when the exercise level is raised, and dims when breathing is depressed.

drives.note: A lobe is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.
Shallow or slow breathing leaves the lobe less ventilated than at rest.

parts.label: Lower Lobe
parts.summary: Right lower lobe, below the oblique fissure
parts.function: The lower lobe is the largest and lies below and behind the oblique fissure, resting on the diaphragm. In an upright body most of the breath is drawn into the lower lobes. Air reaches it through its own lobar bronchus. It brightens when breathing is deeper or faster, for example when the exercise level is raised, and dims when breathing is depressed.

drives.note: A lobe is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.
Shallow or slow breathing leaves the lobe less ventilated than at rest.

parts.label: Bronchial Tree
parts.summary: Lobar bronchi dividing into ever smaller airways
parts.function: The main bronchus divides into lobar bronchi, which divide again and again until the air reaches the terminal airways. These tubes carry air but do not exchange gas, so they make up the anatomical dead space. Air runs in from the hilum while the lung fills and back out while it empties; the stream stops in apnoea, thins when the airways narrow, and the tree takes a warm tint.

drives.note: More air moves through the airways when minute ventilation rises.
Airway narrowing is a direct property of the bronchial smooth muscle.

parts.label: Pulmonary Arteries
parts.summary: Carry oxygen-poor blood from the right heart to the alveoli
parts.function: The pulmonary artery branches alongside the airways and carries all of the cardiac output, oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle, out to the capillaries around the alveoli. In this view the blood is drawn in the venous colour and moves faster when cardiac output is higher; it stops if the heart stops.

drives.note: The whole cardiac output passes through the lungs, so more flow when output rises.

parts.label: Pulmonary Veins
parts.summary: Carry oxygenated blood back to the left atrium
parts.function: The pulmonary veins run between the lung segments, away from the airways, and return freshly oxygenated blood to the left atrium. The stream is drawn in the colour of arterial blood, so it pales towards purple as the oxygen saturation falls.

drives.note: Venous return from the lungs follows cardiac output.
With less oxygen taken up, the blood returning has less oxygen to carry.

parts.label: Alveoli
parts.summary: Air sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged
parts.function: Each smallest airway ends in a cluster of alveoli, thin-walled sacs wrapped in capillaries, where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out. They are drawn far larger than life so the clusters can be seen. They brighten with each inspiration, and dim where blood passes through unventilated lung, which is what a shunt is.

drives.note: Alveolar ventilation is what refreshes the gas in the sacs.
Low arterial oxygen is the signal that the exchange surface is being asked to work harder.
Blood that passes unventilated lung does not take part in exchange.

parts.label: Pleura
parts.summary: The smooth membrane that wraps the lung
parts.function: The visceral pleura covers the lung surface and slides against the lining of the chest wall on a thin film of fluid, which lets the lung follow the chest as it expands. It has no drive of its own in this simulation and is shown for orientation.
